title: A working agent. The next feature.
notes:
Your ADK agent already works. Now you need memory or a browser interface.
Skills give your coding agent an approach to the engineering decisions.

title: Which agent uses the skill?

cards.label: YOUR CODING AGENT
cards.text:
Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity

Reads the skill and your project.
Helps you design, edit and test.

cards.label: YOUR APPLICATION AGENT
cards.text:
The Google ADK program

Runs inside your application.
Responds to your users.

notes: Install skills into the coding client you use to work on the project.

Skills guide development. They do not automatically become
part of the ADK application that your users run.

title: A folder of useful instructions
items: When to use it · how to approach the task
notes: A skill is a small folder your coding agent can read while working.

The coding agent reads relevant material alongside your own code.
The instructions still need to be applied to your particular project.

title: One entry point. Eleven specialists.
notes:
Start with adk-engineer when you know the outcome
but have not chosen a specialist. Three of the eleven are shown here.

It selects the relevant installed instructions. You can also name
a specialist directly. You do not need to have read the book.

title: Begin where your application lives

cards.label: ILLUSTRATIVE EXISTING PROJECT
cards.text:
support-agent/
  agent.py
  database/
  auth/
  tests/
  web/

cards.label: TERMINAL
cards.text:
cd /path/to/support-agent

Use your actual project path.
Keep its existing structure.

notes: Our example already has Python code, a database, login, tests and a React app.

Open a terminal inside your application's project directory.
You do not need to copy the book's example application.

title: A short setup checklist

cards.label: HAVE THESE READY
cards.text:
A coding client that supports skills
Already installed and signed in

Git
Node.js 22.20+ with npm

cards.label: CHECK IN YOUR TERMINAL
cards.text:
git --version
node --version
npm --version

The npm install provides npx.

notes: npx runs the installer that downloads the skill collection.

Downloading the skills needs no cloud credentials.
Your application keeps its own ADK dependencies.

title: Run this in the terminal
notes:
Keep the quotes around '*'. The backslashes continue the command
onto the next line in a macOS or Linux shell.

This downloads the instructions and their supporting files.
Open the same project in your coding agent after installation.

title: The next request goes in chat
notes:
Type the skill request in the coding-agent chat.
If a newly installed skill is missing, start a fresh session.

For Google consumer accounts, use Antigravity.
The README explains supported Gemini CLI access and discovery.

title: 01 / Remember a preferred language
context: Before: a new conversation loses the user's preferred language.
prompt:
/adk-engineer Add memory so our support agent remembers
preferred language between conversations. Reuse our
database and login. Ask before saving; support changes
and forgetting. Add tests for consent and user isolation.
notes: State the outcome, what to reuse, and the behaviours to check.

The entry point selects adk-memory-architecture.
In Codex, replace /adk-engineer with $adk-engineer.

title: Choose what to remember
notes:
The specialist inspects identity, storage interfaces and existing ADK code.
An exact language setting may belong in an ordinary user profile.

Conversation history and document retrieval solve different problems.
Choose the storage to match the information you need.

title: What should the memory tests prove?

cards.label: CONTINUITY & CONSENT
cards.text:
No consent → nothing saved.

A new conversation can load
its user's saved preference.

cards.label: OWNERSHIP & FORGETTING
cards.text:
Other users cannot read it.

Changing or forgetting updates
what later conversations can read.

notes: Ask the coding agent to implement and run these checks in your project.

These are acceptance criteria. Review the actual code and test results;
the diagram does not establish that an implementation passed.

chapter: IV · Add a frontend · Illustrated example
title: 02 / Connect the existing React chat
context: Before: the Python agent works, but the website cannot talk to it.
prompt:
/adk-frontend-integration Connect our React chat to
this ADK agent through an API. Reuse our login.
Stream replies and tool progress. Enforce conversation
ownership. Add API tests and check one browser flow.
notes: Choose the specialist directly when you already know the task.

Preserve the current application. Ask for the connection, ownership
checks and a browser flow that shows the complete result.

chapter: IV · Add a frontend · Illustrated example
title: Connect through your backend
notes: The backend verifies the user and conversation before running the agent.

Your API releases only permitted text and progress.
Use a custom API or AG-UI contract that fits the project.

chapter: IV · Add a frontend · Illustrated example
title: Streaming needs a clear finish
notes: Give text, tool progress, completion and failure distinct meanings.

A final answer should not duplicate text already displayed.
If a request fails after partial text, show that failure.

chapter: IV · Add a frontend · Expected checks
title: Test the whole conversation

cards.label: API & EVENT HANDLING
cards.text:
Users continue only their own chats.

Partial text and tool progress render.
Completion and failure stay distinct.

cards.label: BROWSER FLOW
cards.text:
Send one complete request
through the actual interface.

Report what remains unverified.

notes: Ask for executable checks around the new connection.

Local tests, browser checks and live model evaluation provide different
evidence. These expected checks are not recorded passing results.

title: Combine complementary skills

cards.label: MATT POCOCK'S SKILLS
cards.text:
A development method

Use the installed tdd skill
alongside the ADK specialist.

cards.label: GOOGLE'S AGENTS CLI SKILLS
cards.text:
Project conventions and commands

Use them when working with
an Agents CLI project.

notes:
Both collections are optional. Install them separately and name them
in the request, with a clear scope for the work.

Agents CLI supplies project tools alongside your coding client.
The README has installation steps and combined examples.

title: Give the coding agent direction

cards.label: A USEFUL REQUEST
cards.text:
Outcome: what should change?
Existing code: what should stay?
Boundaries: what must be enforced?
Evidence: how will we check it?

cards.label: A USEFUL REVIEW
cards.text:
Read the diff.
Run the relevant checks.
Inspect the result.
Ask what remains unverified.

notes: Start with one change in a project you already understand.

The skill supplies an approach. You decide whether
the implementation fits your application.

title: Agentic Engineering Skills
notes: Start with adk-engineer and describe the improvement you need.
